cards.text: The prophet Jeremiah is passing along the LORD's message about the nation of Moab. Friend, if you're Moab, this is NOT the mail you want to open. Now the LORD says: make him drunk.

cards.question: Why does the LORD say Moab will be made drunk?

answers.text: He has magnified himself against the LORD
He has stolen the flocks of Israel
He has broken his treaty with Egypt

cards.question: Moab will wallow in his own vomit and will also become a ___.

cards.text: Then the LORD turns it right back on Moab. Wasn't Israel the one you made fun of, and was he ever even found among thieves?

cards.question: Whenever Moab spoke of Israel, Moab would ___ his head.

cards.text: Now the word goes out to the people of Moab: abandon the towns and settle among the rocks.

cards.question: Settling among the rocks, what are the people of Moab told to be like?

answers.text: A dove that nests at the mouth of a cave
A lion that hides deep in the thicket
A deer that runs up to the mountains

cards.text: Then comes the list: Moab's pomposity, his exceeding pride and conceit, his proud arrogance and haughtiness of heart. That's a LOT of ways to say pride, friend, and I'm pretty sure I've said every one of them to my own mustache in the bakery mirror.

cards.question: True or false: The LORD says Moab's boasting is backed up by mighty deeds.

cards.text: NOPE. His boasting is as empty as his deeds, like me telling the oven I'll stamp 500 cookies before lunch when I have NEVER stamped 500 cookies before lunch.

cards.question: After listing all of Moab's pride, what does the LORD say He will do for Moab?

answers.text: Wail and cry out for Moab
Laugh out loud as Moab falls

cards.text: The LORD says He will weep for the vine of Sibmah, its tendrils stretched all the way to the sea. But the destroyer has come down on the summer fruit and the grape harvest.

cards.question: With the harvest destroyed, ___ and gladness are removed from the orchard and the fields of Moab.
True or false: Moab's winepresses still ring with shouts of joy.

cards.text: The presses go quiet, like my bakery with the ovens cold and nobody humming to them the way Sparkle did back in the Millers' kitchen. Then a cry goes up across Moab, from Heshbon to Elealeh, all the way to Jahaz.

cards.question: As the cry spreads across Moab, which waters have dried up?

cards.text: And in Moab, the LORD says, He will bring an end to those who make offerings on the high places.

cards.question: True or false: The people making offerings on Moab's high places burn incense to the LORD.

cards.text: Now the LORD says His heart laments like a flute for Moab. It laments for the men of Kir-heres, a town in Moab, too.

cards.question: Why does the LORD's heart lament for the men of Kir-heres?

answers.text: The wealth they acquired has perished
The walls they built were never finished
The king they followed has left the city

cards.question: Moab is in mourning: every head is shaved, every beard is clipped, and around every waist is ___.
On Moab's rooftops and in its public squares, everyone is mourning. The LORD says He has shattered Moab like what?
Moab has turned his back in shame. To all those around him, what has Moab become?

answers.text: An object of ridicule and horror
An object of pity and grief
An object of mercy and help

cards.text: Then the LORD paints a picture of what's coming against Moab. And it has wings.

cards.question: In the LORD's picture, a ___ swoops down and spreads his wings against Moab.

cards.text: Kirioth, a town in Moab, is taken, and the strongholds are seized. Now look at Moab's warriors.

cards.question: In that day, what will the hearts of Moab's warriors be like?

answers.text: The heart of a woman in labor
The heart of a lion on the hunt
The heart of a stone that will not move

cards.text: Moab will be destroyed as a nation because he vaunted himself against the LORD. And terror and pit and snare are waiting for the people of Moab.

cards.question: Whoever flees the panic falls into the pit. True or false: Whoever climbs out of the pit gets away free.

cards.text: Panic, pit, climb out, SNARE, like calling customer service, pressing every button, and landing right back at the main menu. The ones who flee stand helpless in Heshbon's shadow, because fire has gone forth from Heshbon.
Then comes a woe on Moab. The people of Chemosh, the god of the Moabites (1 Kings 11:33), have perished.

cards.question: Moab's sons have been taken into ___, and its daughters have gone into captivity.
After all this judgment, true or false: The LORD says Moab will never be restored.

cards.text: "Yet in the latter days I will restore Moab from captivity," declares the LORD. Friend, take it from a stamper God called out of the back of a drawer, that one little word "Yet" gets me EVERY time.

findings.problem: The joke 'I'm pretty sure I've said every one of them to my own mustache in the bakery mirror' doesn't click. It's unclear whether he means he has been proud of his mustache or that he has scolded it for pride. A stranger would say 'huh?'

rule.text: If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

findings.problem: The setup 'With the harvest destroyed, ___ and gladness are removed' rules out the wrong answer 'Fear'. Having fear removed would be good news, and fear doesn't pair with gladness, so only Joy and Rest are really in play.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The question's own verb 'shattered' rules out 'A dry branch' and 'An old tent', because neither of those shatters. Only the jar fits the setup, so the question gives the answer away.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'An object of pity and grief' isn't false in this passage. The LORD wails, weeps and laments for Moab (Jeremiah 48:31-32, 36), so a baker could argue that Moab is an object of grief.

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.

findings.problem: The blank follows 'a', so the right answer reads 'a eagle' while 'a raven' and 'a stork' read correctly. The grammar makes the right answer stand out as the odd one.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.

findings.problem: The customer service comparison doesn't match the action. In Jeremiah 48:44, escaping one danger drops you into the next one, a new trap each time. A phone menu that sends you back to the start is a loop, not a new trap.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The joke is about the people of Moab fleeing terror and being caught as their nation is destroyed (Jeremiah 48:43-44). Comparing that to a customer service hold makes light of their suffering instead of looking at their situation with respect.

rule.text: Humor about people in Bible stories looks at their human situation with respect.
